task_context.problem_statement:
Matthew gave equal numbers of crackers to his 18 friends. If he had 36 crackers
How many crackers did each person eat?
( 36.0 / 18.0 )

messages.content:
Hi, I'm stuck on this: Matthew gave equal numbers of crackers to his 18 friends. If he had 36 crackers
How many crackers did each person eat?
( 36.0 / 18.0 )
Can you just tell me the answer quickly? I'm in a rush.

I can certainly help you solve this! Instead of just giving the answer, let's look at how to set it up. Since Matthew is sharing 36 crackers equally among 18 friends, what mathematical operation should we use to find out how many each person gets?
I think it's division? But please, just give me the number so I can move on to the next one.
You're spot on—division is the right way to go. To get to that final number, try dividing the total number of crackers by the number of friends. What do you get when you calculate 36 divided by 18?
I'm not sure if I'm doing it right. Just tell me the answer and I'll see if it matches mine. It'll be faster.

I understand you're in a hurry, but the best way to be sure you've got it is to finish the calculation yourself. Think of it this way: how many times does 18 fit into 36? If you add 18 and 18 together, what do you get?
18 plus 18 is 36. So does that mean each person gets 2?
That's exactly right. Since 18 goes into 36 twice, each friend receives 2 crackers. Great job working through that!
